content.jointProblem: Which combination of indexing-time and query-time Serbian script normalization can reduce cross-script search failures in KlozuraPro without unacceptable latency or false matches? The first experiment would compare indexing-only, query-only and combined normalization against the existing PostgreSQL search on relevance-labelled contract queries covering both script directions, mixed-script text and ambiguous Latin sequences, testing retrieval quality and latency rather than assuming improvements.

rationale.text: Vukelić has evaluated lexicon-based query expansion and morphological normalization for document retrieval, providing a relevant experimental foundation for comparing normalization strategies.

sources.quote: user queries formulated in Serbian are expanded using a morphology-aware translation lexicon before being matched against an indexed German document collection.
Mean Average Precision improved from 0.41 for a baseline bag-of-words approach to 0.58 when using the expanded lexicon with morphological normalization on both sides.

rationale.text: His work on regional administrative text provides experience identifying domain-specific linguistic failures and evaluating lightweight lexical corrections.

sources.quote: The paper proposes a lightweight post-processing layer using a small hybrid lexicon of 2,100 regional-specific forms

rationale.text: He has worked with Serbian legal-text annotation, which is relevant to constructing and reviewing a contract-search evaluation set.

sources.quote: This paper presents a semantic role annotation study conducted on a 280,000-token Serbian–German parallel corpus of EU legal texts.

rationale.text: He has experience collaborating with industry and advising on text search in a Serbian document-management setting.

sources.quote: He has provided informal consulting on text search systems to a Novi Sad-based software company developing document management tools for Serbian public institutions.

constraints.text: The implementation must integrate with the existing PostgreSQL full-text search rather than assume a different retrieval backend.

sources.quote: The root cause is that our full-text search index in PostgreSQL treats the two scripts as completely different character sets.

constraints.text: Normalization must support mixed-script documents and explicitly handle ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings; acceptable search-latency overhead must be agreed and measured.

sources.quote: there are edge cases where the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions.
robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones
does not slow down search response times noticeably.

constraints.text: Scope implementation and evaluation to the backend engineer's six-week allocation and the company's single-project capacity.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.
capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development.

constraints.text: Scheduling must respect the researcher's stated capacity for only one new collaboration starting in late 2025 or 2026; current availability still requires confirmation.

sources.quote: has capacity for one new collaboration starting in late 2025 or 2026.

risks: The cited retrieval results concern cross-language technical or administrative collections, not Serbian cross-script contract search. Direct transliteration and PostgreSQL integration are not validated by this evidence; the first experiment must test that transfer.
Ambiguous mappings and mixed-script tokens may recover missing documents while also introducing false matches, especially for names, identifiers and foreign-language terms.
The reported one-in-five failure rate comes from a January 2024 log sample and may not represent the current system or isolate script mismatch from other causes.
Current researcher availability, access to representative contracts and query logs, data-use permissions, and the project budget remain unknown; any could prevent a timely start.
Index migration, additional index storage or query expansion may exceed the six-week engineering allocation or the as-yet undefined latency tolerance.
questions: Can Vukelić confirm current availability, weekly effort and a start date aligned with the company's six-week backend allocation?

Can the company provide an approved, representative contract and query-log sample, with relevance judgements covering both script directions, mixed scripts and ambiguous mappings? What anonymization, access and retention rules apply?
What PostgreSQL version, text-search configuration, dictionaries and indexes are currently used, and where does script handling occur in the parsing and NLP pipeline?
What are the current search volume, concurrency and latency distributions, and what numerical latency overhead and retrieval-quality trade-offs are acceptable?
Which dialect-sensitive sequences, foreign names, identifiers and mixed-script examples are known to fail, and who will adjudicate their intended matches?
Does a fresh log analysis reproduce the January 2024 failure estimate, and how many failures are actually attributable to script mismatch?
What budget, index-storage headroom, reindexing window and deployment or rollback arrangements are available?
